## 2026-08-26 ~9:45pm PDT — ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **JAKE COMPLETES HIS 8/24 POLICY-PUT QUESTION INTO A FULL DESIGN: A TREASURY-DEMAND STABILIZER SPV — pre-designated IG eligibility (no purchase promise) · SPV-owned CDX protection whose harvested gains BUY TREASURIES on moderate widening · a finite, competitively-auctioned corporate purchase window on severe widening (>~250bp) · recycling on normalization. Objective: stop sovereign and AI-corporate issuance from bidding against each other for the same marginal duration dollar** — filed as HIS DESIGN, graded below both ways
Source: Jake's concept document, 8/26 evening — the fully-worked version of the 8/24 question
this note answered with the SMCCF template (`:L7362`). His design explicitly targets the vault's
duration-collision mechanism (today's issuance-ladder entry; the 7Y branch).

### GRADING (analysis; the design is Jake's)
**WHAT IS GENUINELY STRONG:**
- **★★★★ The diagnosis is this board's own: two sovereign-scale issuers competing for one
  marginal duration buyer** — his §14 loop IS the collision branch, independently derived.
- **★★★★ Eligibility-without-commitment + scarcity + reverse auction is a real improvement on
  the 2020 template's moral hazard** — and his §11 front-running multiplier is EXACTLY what
  2020 proved: ~$14B bought against $750B capacity, spreads collapsed on ANNOUNCEMENT (~2%
  utilisation). His design would run on expectation, as the SMCCF did.
- **★★★★ THE SLEEPER FEATURE IS §1's DISCLOSURE PRICE: making SPV/RVG/residual-value/guarantee
  disclosure the cost of eligibility would force exactly the transparency this board excavates
  quarterly — implementable ALONE, without any purchase leg, and arguably the best piece.**
- **⭐ Recycling (§12) has precedent: the SMCCF wound down at a profit.**
- **⭐ Chassis note: as designed this is a TREASURY instrument (SPV equity, ESF-class capital),
  not a Fed one — consistent with the week's administered-30Y finding: the long-end policy arm
  is already Treasury.**

**⛔ THE COUNTERS, argued because they are load-bearing:**
1. **THE CDS LEG HEDGES THE SYSTEM AGAINST ITSELF FROM INSIDE. Who sells the SPV protection at
   universe scale? Dealers and the PE-insurance complex — the same balance sheets holding the
   corporate credit. In the stress state, the SPV's harvested gains are THEIR realized losses:
   the facility extracts capital FROM the credit system DURING the stress to buy Treasuries —
   counter-cyclical for the sovereign, PRO-cyclical for credit. The stabilizer destabilizes the
   market it is watching.** And the sovereign officially positioned SHORT its own corporate
   sector is signal-toxic: disclosure of the hedge book could itself widen spreads — §11's
   front-running runs both directions.
2. **A UNIVERSE-LEVEL PUT IS STILL A PUT. §9's no-security-specific-put discipline is real, but
   2020's lesson cuts against §4: eligibility ≈ guarantee in market pricing — spreads repriced
   on the announcement, before any bond was bought or any auction run. The competitive window
   design would be capitalized into eligible-bond prices on DAY ONE**, cheapening exactly the
   AI-IG issuance the facility exists to stop crowding out Treasuries — partially self-defeating.
3. **THE RELATIVE-VALUE PREMISE IS THE WEAKEST LINK: this week's own data says Treasury yields
   are being driven by the POLICY PATH (belly +80bp/6mo) and supply, not primarily by IG
   competition — and the fix for corporate-supply crowding involves the sovereign ABSORBING the
   AI-credit risk the market was correctly repricing.** The weary-rotation thesis inverts under
   this facility: hedged Treasuries + capped corporate widening REMOVES the asymmetry that makes
   rotation rational — it would suppress the exact repricing the board's base case expects, at
   the cost of socializing the tail.
4. **The eligibility line reproduces 2020's: IG-only. The periphery (CCC 1,036bp, neoclouds,
   CRWV) stays outside — the put again protects the calm stages and abandons the stressed one.**
   Consistent with this board's standing conclusion; his design inherits it knowingly.
**NET: as POLICY, the disclosure-for-eligibility piece is excellent and severable; the CDS leg
is the novel part and the broken part; the purchase window is the SMCCF with better auction
mechanics and the same announcement-effect economics.** **AS A MARKET TELL: file the design's
EXISTENCE as evidence — this is the second time in 72 hours the policy-put architecture has
been independently reinvented at this desk. When a structure keeps getting rediscovered, its
eventual official version is closer than the calm implies. The SMCCF-template forest branch
carries the watch.**
**📌** (1) any official trial balloon resembling this (Treasury/Fed speeches, Jackson Hole
included — Warsh Friday); (2) the §1 disclosure-mandate idea as standalone policy chatter.

### Addendum 2026-08-26 ~9:52pm PDT — **JAKE'S REFINEMENT FLIPS THE CDS LEG AND DISSOLVES COUNTER #1: TREASURY IS THE PROTECTION WRITER, NOT THE BUYER — it SELLS the credit protection (collecting premium in calm, supplying loss-absorption in stress) — and the intervention pool is UNIFIED AND CONDITIONAL: the same capital goes to Treasury buybacks OR corporate purchases "where the market points it," instead of mechanically buying billions of Treasuries back on schedule**
- **CONCEDED: the counterparty objection dies in this version.** Treasury-as-writer doesn't drain
  dealer/insurer capital in stress — it supplies it. And **the unified conditional pool is the
  design's strongest piece: the vault's own critique of the current buyback program (administered
  30Y, ≥$4B/op on schedule regardless of conditions) is that it's mechanical. One
  state-contingent facility with two nozzles — sovereign or corporate, allocated by the
  relative-value break — is strictly more efficient per dollar than the scheduled version
  Treasury runs today.** It also PRICES the put 2020 gave away free: the implicit backstop
  exists either way (SMCCF proved it); selling it captures premium and defines terms —
  the FDIC/TRIA precedent class. *(Analysis.)*
- **⛔ THE TWO PROBLEMS THAT REPLACE THE ONE THAT DIED:**
  **(1) WRONG-WAY RISK, contractual: the sovereign's payout obligation peaks at the exact moment
  its own funding costs peak.** Discretionary puts (2020) let the state choose its moment;
  written protection pays out on the correlation event by contract — the AI-credit tail lands on
  the Treasury precisely when the belly is selling off. Premium income is calm-state comfort;
  the S&L/2008 deposit-insurance asymmetry is the precedent's dark side.
  **(2) ADVERSE-SELECTION PRICING: Treasury-insured corporates become quasi-sovereign + spread —
  MORE attractive than Treasuries, defeating the crowding objective — unless the premium eats
  most of the spread, at which point nobody buys protection in calm and everyone buys it in
  stress.** The insurance death spiral is the design constraint; pricing it is the whole game.
- **⭐ Legal chassis note: buybacks are statutory (31 USC 3111); Treasury-written derivatives at
  scale and direct corporate purchases need ESF stretch or Congress — the 2020 Treasury-equity/
  Fed-leverage split existed precisely to route around this.** *(Analysis.)*
- **The meta-tell strengthens: the refinement converges the design toward what Treasury is
  ALREADY half-doing (administered long end, conditional support). "Where the market points it"
  is one legislative step from current practice.** Warsh Friday, watched with this on file.

#### Addendum 2026-08-26 ~10:00pm PDT — **JAKE'S SECOND REFINEMENT: THE HEDGE LEG'S CONVEXITY *IS* THE WAR CHEST — as spreads widen the protection leg gains mark-to-market, gets SOLD in the secondary market, and the proceeds fund the bid (buybacks or corporates); then a NEW hedge is struck AT-ISSUANCE/AT-THE-MONEY, carrying no accrued spread value — the book resets and re-arms.** ✅ **CONCEDED: this kills the funding half of the wrong-way objection. The facility never needs to raise money at the worst moment — the widening itself mints the intervention capital, mechanically, before the intervention is needed. Self-financing countercyclicality is the design's elegant core and it survives every round of this argument.**
- **The two residuals that remain (smaller, but real):**
  **(1) HARVEST LIQUIDITY: selling appreciated index protection in the stress state is selling
  into a one-way market — everyone wants protection exactly when the facility is selling it.
  Realized will run below marked; the war chest is worth less at the moment of use than on the
  screen.** (Mitigant: index CDX is the most liquid credit instrument there is; this is a
  haircut, not a refutation.)
  **(2) SOMEONE IS STILL SHORT THE HARVESTED LEG. The netting is the fix and the remaining
  design constraint: if Treasury BOTH writes protection (to real-money hedgers — who get PAID
  in stress, stabilizing) and holds its long hedge leg, the book runs near-matched with a
  modest long-protection tilt, premiums carrying the tilt. The state becomes a credit-risk
  CLEARINGHOUSE with a countercyclical lean — the net drain on private balance sheets shrinks
  to the tilt, not the notional.** Roll cost noted: re-striking at-the-money after harvest means
  high running premium at wide spreads — the re-arm is expensive when calm returns.
- **Standing: the design is now internally coherent — priced put + self-funding hedge +
  conditional two-nozzle deployment + at-the-money resets. What remains are execution
  parameters (tilt size, premium pricing vs adverse selection, harvest haircuts), not
  structural breaks.** *(Jake's design; grading analysis.)*

### THESIS (interpretation — NOT fact)
- **★★★★★ THE ANSWER (gopher's frame, adopted and sharpened): SELL THE RESIDUAL, KEEP THE
  TOLL.** The emerging model: originate → build → securitize → insurer/ABS/wealth holds the
  duration → manager keeps origination/servicing/management fees → equity recycles into the
  next vintage. **They exit the RISK while compounding the BUSINESS. If the cycle cracks,
  losses land on policyholders, annuitants, ABS buyers and LPs — the manager's P&L keeps
  the fees either way.** This is the Burry chain (arrows 4-12, on file since May) restated
  from the SPONSOR'S side: what looks like his warning from the holders' seat is a business
  model from the originators' seat. *(Analysis.)*
- **★★★★ THE SELECTION-BIAS CUT (the strongest anti-GTFO evidence, held honestly):** with
  52% of inventory stuck >4yrs and distributions at lows, they are not choosing to sell —
  they are selling WHAT THE BID WANTS, and the bid wants AI-infra (CoolIT 15x, stabilized
  DCs, insurance distribution). The exits are price-taking, not a doom signal. **BUT the
  buyer of that bid is partly the conveyor itself** — the insurance/ABS/wealth complex the
  same firms built — which is how a top gets financed by its own distribution system.
  *(Analysis.)*
- **★★★★ THE COUNTER-NUANCE, filed so the thesis stays honest: KKR IS NOT FULLY DE-RISKED.
  Global Atlantic is WHOLLY OWNED** — $164B of credit at the captive insurer IS KKR
  balance-sheet exposure. The clean version of the model (Apollo/Athene similar) keeps the
  duration inside the family at the regulated subsidiary. The de-risking is real at the
  FUND level and partial at the FIRM level — which is exactly why Bessent's May meeting
  and the NAIC/Delaware branch matter: the captive is where the recycling stops.
  *(Analysis.)*
- **★★★ THE DISCRIMINATOR, REGISTERED AS THE WATCH (gopher's close, adopted):** the bearish
  tell is NOT headline exits — it is **sponsors repeatedly selling equity/residual risk
  while retaining only origination/management economics, as insurers/annuities/ABS/retail
  absorb the duration.** Blackstone selling under-construction-but-leased DCs + the FT's
  SRT/softening item are the first two entries in that column. *(Analysis.)*
